L118: ### 2025 Taiwan-Hungary Seminar & Business Matchmaking Event
L119: 
L120: Unlock Boundless Opportunities in Smart Cities—Are You Ready to Forge New Partnerships?
L121: 
L122: The Budapest Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BKIK) and the Hungarian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (MKIK) will lead a delegation of 10 Hungarian companies to Taiwan in March 2025. Together with the Taiwan External Trade Development Council (TAITRA), they will co-host the " 2025 Taiwan-Hungary Seminar & Business Matchmaking Event " on March 19.
L123: This event aims to foster collaboration between Taiwan and Hungary, enhancing industry partnerships in smart cities and related fields to create future development opportunities.
L124: 
L125: Event Details:
L126: 
L127: Date: March 19, 2025 (Wednesday)
L128: 
L129: Venue: Room 504BC, 5F, Taipei Nangang Exhibition Center, Hall 1
L130: 
L131: This event features two key sessions:
L132: 
L133: Seminar
L134: Hear from leading Taiwanese and Hungarian companies on smart city solutions, including cybersecurity software, smart/green building materials, and telematics applications. Experts will provide insights into market trends.
L135: 
L136: 1-on-1 Business Matchmaking
L137: 
L138: Engage in face-to-face discussions with Hungarian companies. This dedicated matchmaking session will help businesses explore partnerships, technology exchanges, and cooperation opportunities.
L139: 
L140: Tentative Agenda:
L141: Time  | Session  | Notes
L142: 08:30-09:00
L143:  | Registration
L144:  |
L145: 09:00-10:00
L146:  | Taiwan-Hungary Seminar
L147:  | 1. Introduction of 10 Hungarian companies
L148: 2. Presentations from Taiwanese industry associations
L149: 10:00-12:00
L150:  | 1-on-1 Business Matchmaking  | Each meeting lasts 20 minutes
L151: 
L152: The organizers reserve the right to adjust the event content and schedule.
L153:

L100: # FOREIGN TRADE IN GOODS OF THE REPUBLIC OF CROATIA − Provisional Data January – May 2025 and January – June 2025
L101: 
L102: According to provisional data, from January to May 2025, the total export of the Republic of Croatia amounted to 10.2 billion euro. At the same time, total import was 18.4 billion euro. Foreign trade deficit amounted to 8.1 billion euro.
L103: 
L104: In the period from January to May 2025, coverage of import by export was 55.7%.
L105: According to the First Results, in the period from January to June 2025, the total export of the Republic of Croatia amounted to 12.3 billion euro, while total import was 22.0 billion euro. Foreign trade deficit amounted to 9.7 billion euro.
L106: 
L107: According to the First Results, the coverage of import by export was 55.9% from January to June 2025.

L51: President Lai meets delegation from Estonian parliamentary Foreign Affairs Committee
L52: 
L53: 【23†President Lai meets delegation from Estonian parliamentary Foreign Affairs Committee
L54: †www.youtube.com】
L55: On the afternoon of November 1, President Lai Ching-te met with a delegation from the Foreign Affairs Committee of the Riigikogu (Parliament of Estonia). In remarks, President Lai thanked Estonia for staunchly supporting Taiwan’s international participation and said that Taiwan has the responsibility, the ability, and the willingness to contribute even more to the international community in every domain.
L56: The president expressed his hope that we can work together to continue deepening the partnership between Taiwan and Estonia, and that by strengthening cooperation with European Union member states across many areas, we can jointly respond to the challenges posed by expanding authoritarianism, thereby safeguarding global peace, stability, and prosperity.
L57: A translation of President Lai’s remarks follows:
L58: 
L59: I extend a warm welcome to our good friends from the Foreign Affairs Committee of the Riigikogu. This is Chairman Marko Mihkelson’s second visit to Taiwan. He visited last August with a delegation of parliamentary foreign affairs committee chairs from the Baltic states. Members of the Riigikogu Ester Karuse and Luisa Rõivas are also visiting again, having been part of a delegation led by Estonia-Taiwan Support Group Chairman Kristo Enn Vaga in March.
L60: Your presence here demonstrates that Taiwan-Estonia relations are growing closer. I believe that with your support and assistance, our alliance, based on the shared values of freedom and democracy, and our economic and trade partnership are sure to grow even stronger. For this, I express my sincere gratitude.
L61: The international landscape and geopolitical environment are changing rapidly. Expanding authoritarianism is challenging the universal values of freedom and democracy as well as the rules-based international order. At this critical juncture, it is even more imperative that like-minded nations unite and work together to safeguard global peace, stability, and prosperity.
L62: In addition to strengthening cooperation with other nations to defend the values of freedom and democracy, Taiwan has actively sought inclusion in such international organizations and mechanisms as the World Health Organization, the International Civil Aviation Organization, and the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change.
L63: More than just a matter of the fundamental human rights of the 23 million people of Taiwan, it demonstrates that Taiwan has the responsibility, the ability, and the willingness to contribute even more to the international community in every domain.

L80: ## 甚麼是戰略性高科技貨品
L81: 
L82: 2026-02-11 貿易安全管理辦公室
L83: 戰略性高科技貨品(Strategic High-Tech Commodities, SHTC)，係指戰略性高科技貨品輸出管制清單內貨品（包括：軍商兩用貨品及技術出口管制清單、一般軍用貨品清單、輸往北韓敏感貨品清單、輸往伊朗敏感貨品清單、輸往俄羅斯及白俄羅斯高科技貨品清單等），或非屬前述清單內項目，惟最終用途或最終使用者有可能用於生產、發展核子、生化、飛彈等軍事武器用途者（包括：交易對象屬我國公告之【58†戰略性高科技貨品出口實體管理名單†publicinfo.trade.gov.tw】等異常交易情形），或依出口國政府規定須取得我國核發國際進口證明書或其他相關保證文件之輸入貨品。
L84: 戰略性高科技貨品未經許可，不得輸出。如未經許可出口前述管制貨品將因違反貿易法而面臨有期徒刑、拘役、科或併科罰金或罰鍰、停止輸出、輸入或輸出入貨品或撤銷進出口廠商登記等裁罰。
L85: 軍商兩用貨品及技術出口管制清單將前述管制貨品分為10大類別，包括：核能物質與設施、特殊材料與相關設備、材料加工程序、電子、電腦、電信及資訊安全、感應器與雷射、導航與航空電子、海事、航太與推進系統等。（【59†戰略性高科技貨品鑑定諮詢†shtc.org.tw】）
